manifest.title: Lathe
manifest.author: Adam Smith
manifest.description: Coding agent tools (lathe, bash, read, write, edit, glob, grep, view, interpret, delegate, onboard, expose, destroy) backed by per-user sandbox VMs with transparent lifecycle management.

specs.name: bash
specs.description:
Execute a bash command in the sandbox. Non-interactive only.
Commands that finish within the foreground window return output directly.
Long-running commands auto-background and return a descriptor with log
file paths for monitoring. Text previews are capped at 50 KiB. Full logs and
exit status remain readable for 24 hours after completion, until a later
bash call reaps expired evidence. Sandbox stop/restart clears these files.

When creating git commits, add an Assisted-by: Lathe trailer to the
commit message to acknowledge AI assistance.

foreground_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before auto-backgrounding. Omit or set -1 to use the server default. Set 0 for immediate background (fire-and-forget). Use higher positive values for known-slow commands.

specs.name: delegate
specs.description:
Run bounded autonomous work with the same model and shared sandbox.
Has bash/read/write/edit/glob/grep, not user interaction or expose.
Returns a summary or background sidecar paths; see lathe(manpage="delegate").

task.description: Specific goal, constraints, and findings; the sub-agent cannot ask questions.

context_files.description: Absolute sandbox reference files; missing or aggregate >50 KiB (including headings/separators) fails before inference, never silently clips.

max_steps.description: Inference-call budget, 1–30 (default 10). At 1, no tools: supplied-context analysis only. Use >=2 for sandbox work.

foreground_seconds.description: Wait before auto-backgrounding, 0–300 seconds; 0 backgrounds immediately, -1 uses default 30.

specs.name: destroy
specs.description:
Permanently destroy the sandbox VM. Irreversible.
Prompts the user for confirmation before proceeding.
If a persistent volume is attached, its data is preserved and will reappear in the next sandbox.

specs.name: edit
specs.description: Edit a file by exact string replacement. Fails on ambiguous matches unless replace_all=true.

specs.name: expose
specs.description:
Expose a sandbox service. Named targets manage startup and recovery;
http:<port> requires an already-running service. ttyd and code-server are private-only.

target.description: "dufs" or "dufs:/absolute/path" for file transfer, "site:/absolute/path" for static files, "ttyd" for a shell, "code-server" or "code-server:/absolute/path" for an IDE, or "http:<port>" for an existing service (port 3000–9999). Named directory roots must be within /home/daytona/workspace; bare names use the workspace. An IDE root is not filesystem confinement.

access.description: Required policy: "private" authenticates the owner and fails closed; "public" allows anyone with the URL and may fall back to a direct bearer URL. Choose private unless the user explicitly requests public/world access.

tag.description: Optional untrusted hostname hint, such as "vscode" or "files": lowercase letters, digits, and internal hyphens, max 32 characters. The deployment may ignore it. Hostname text never proves identity or purpose.

upstream_headers.description: Optional fixed application headers for HTTP and WebSocket forwarding, independent of public/private access. Replaces browser values case-insensitively; supports Authorization. Requires a compatible wrapper, with no direct fallback. Max 16 headers, 64-byte names, printable ASCII values up to 4096 bytes, 8192 bytes total. Routing/transport headers are forbidden. Values remain in tool arguments; see lathe(manpage="services") for trust boundaries.

specs.name: glob
specs.description:
Search for files in the sandbox workspace by glob pattern.
Returns concrete absolute paths and an exact count of discovered files.
Scans the full scope, but retains at most max_lines paths. The header
reports omissions; narrow the pattern to see other files. Truncated
results are a traversal-order sample, not a globally sorted prefix.

pattern.description: Comma-separated globs, !-prefix to exclude. Supports *, ?, character classes, and ** as a complete component for directory recursion; brace expansion is not supported. Examples: '**/*.py', 'src/**/*.ts,!**/node_modules/**'.

max_lines.description: Max concrete result lines, excluding the summary header (default: 100, clamped to 1–500).

specs.name: grep
specs.description:
Search file contents in the sandbox workspace by regex.
Returns concrete absolute path:line: text hits and counts of matching
lines and files. Scans the full scope, skipping binary/unreadable files,
but retains at most max_lines hits (text clipped to 200 characters).
The header reports omissions; narrow files or pattern to see other hits.
Truncated results are a traversal-order sample, not a representative one.

files.description: File scope as comma-separated globs (default: '**/*'). !-prefix to exclude. Supports *, ?, character classes, and ** as a complete component for directory recursion; brace expansion is not supported.

max_lines.description: Max concrete result lines, excluding the summary header (default: 100, clamped to 1–500).

specs.name: handoff
specs.description: Get formatting instructions for a user-approved handoff to a fresh chat. Write it as reply text, then end this response; later user requests may continue here.

specs.name: interpret
specs.description:
Run Python code in a persistent REPL session. Variables, imports, and
definitions survive across calls within the same conversation.
Use this for iterative data exploration, incremental computation, or
any workflow where you need state to persist between executions.
For one-shot shell commands or non-Python work, prefer bash() instead.
Stream output is a 50 KiB preview; excess output is discarded explicitly.
Write large results to a sandbox file for full access via read() or expose().

code.description: Python code to execute. Top-level await is not supported.

timeout.description: Max execution time in seconds (default: 120). Use 0 for no limit.

specs.name: lathe
specs.description: Read operational orientation or a task-specific manual page.

manpage.description: "overview" for safeguards and page index; "interpret", "delegate", "background", "services", "egress", "handoff" for details; "version" for installed version.

specs.name: onboard
specs.description:
Load project listing, AGENTS.md, and skill catalog; also searches ~/.agents/.
Read relevant SKILL.md files for full instructions. Skip repeat onboarding
when the supplied context already covers this project.

specs.name: read
specs.description:
Read a file from the sandbox. Returns numbered lines, capped at 2000 lines
and 50 KiB of text. A clipped preview is explicitly labeled; the original
file remains available via bash byte ranges or expose().
Supports Python-style negative indexing: start=-10 reads from
10 lines before the end, stop=-3 stops 3 lines before the end.
All positive values are 1-indexed. stop is exclusive (half-open).
stop=0 (default) means end of file.

start.description: First line to return (1-indexed). Negative counts from end. 0 is treated as 1.

stop.description: Line to stop before (exclusive, 1-indexed). Negative counts from end. 0 means end of file.

specs.name: view
specs.description:
View an image file from the sandbox, loading it into your visual context.
Use for screenshots, charts, rendered pages, or generated images.
Requires a vision-capable model; if the current model cannot accept image
input, the call is refused with a reminder instead of the image.
Supported formats: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP (detected from file contents, not
extension). Max 4 MB; downscale larger images first via bash (e.g. with
ImageMagick or Pillow).

path.description: Absolute path to the image file.

specs.name: write
specs.description:
Write a file to the sandbox (creates parents automatically).

For large files, prefer a skeleton-then-edit workflow: write the file first
with overall structure and ``# PLACEHOLDER: <section>`` markers, then use
``edit()`` to expand each placeholder incrementally. This makes progress
visible to the user in real time and keeps partial work on disk if
generation is interrupted.
